newsitem.title: USA: Israelis play down tiff over Palestinian committee.
newsitem.headline: Israelis play down tiff over Palestinian committee.

text.p: Israeli diplomats sought on Friday to play down a diplomatic tiff with the U.S. State Department over U.S. comments seen by Israel as bolstering the status of the Palestinian Authority.

The dispute centred on remarks Monday by department spokesman Nicholas Burns announcing creation of a joint U.S.-Palestinian commission. Burns compared the body to commissions the United States has with Russia, Egypt and South Africa.

Israeli officials said this was seen as implying that the Palestinian Authority was on a par with full-fledged states, and ambassador Eliahu Ben Elissar had called on U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross to express "deep disappointment".
The officials quoted Ben Elissar as telling Israeli journalists at a briefing Thursday that Ross had told him that Burns had gone beyond his instructions in making the comparison.
Burns defended himself Friday, referring to what he called the "very surprising press conference" by Ben Elissar.
"Everything that I said this week on the U.S.-Palestinian Committee is obviously ... U.S. policy," he told a news briefing.

Ross was not immediately available for comment, but Burns told reporters later: "Dennis and I are on the same sheet of music. Dennis supports everything I said this week ... I just assume (Ben Elissar) must have been confused by the facts yesterday."
U.S. officials said Ben Elissar had subsequently telephoned Burns and apologised for "some of these remarks".
And in a further conciliatory gesture, Israeli embassy spokesman Gadi Baltiansky described Burns as "one of the finest diplomats that I have ever met".

The joint commission, to be headed by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, is largely intended to smooth the flow of U.S. economic aid to the Palestinians.

Burns described the U.S.-Palestinian relationship as "exceedingly important to the United States ... The value of that relationship for the Israelis is that if the Palestinians can be a good, consistent negotiating partner to the state of Israel, then everybody benefits."
